## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle iconographic *yíguǐ* 儀軌 on the construction (造) of the **Sahasrabhuja-Avalokiteśvara** image, attributed to **Śubhakarasiṃha** ([善無畏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%96%84%E7%84%A1%E7%95%8F)) of central India (中天竺國三藏). The text functions as a craftsman's manual coupled with a ritual-consecration manual: it gives the iconographic specifications for sculpting, painting, or modelling the deity, ordered in a definite sequence (次第).

**Abstract**

The opening describes the central image: 上首正體身大黃色 — "the principal embodied figure is golden-yellow in color" — seated cross-legged on a great jewelled lotus pedestal, the lotus having thirty-two principal petals each with smaller leaves between them, each leaf adorned with countless mahā-maṇi gems. The chief face of the deity is then described, with the supplementary heads (eleven-headed iconography), the forty-two principal arms each with their attribute (the *vajra*, the *cintāmaṇi*, the *padma*, the *cakra*, the bow and arrow, the willow branch, the noose, etc.), the colors and *mudrā* of each, and the maṇḍala-attendants. The text is the locus classicus for the iconographic specification of the Sahasrabhuja deity in Tángmì practice and represents the **Śubhakarasiṃha** lineage's approach — distinct from but harmonious with the **Vajrabodhi** / **Amoghavajra** lineage manuals ([KR6j0255](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0255), [KR6j0273](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0273)). It is one of the most-cited *yíguǐ* in subsequent Japanese Shingon sculptural traditions concerning the *Senjū-Kannon* (千手觀音).
